userStories.title: Tracked repository list and search tools
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement safe, bounded tracked-file listing and git grep tools for thread sessions.

**Motivation** — Claude's `read` mode has no Grep or Glob, D544, so the agent needs code-search tools without disturbing PLAN and RUN jobs.

**Approach** — `ThreadToolContext = { worktree: string; skillsRoot: string; skills: ThreadSkillSource[]; git: Git; searchTimeoutMs: number; nowMs: () => number }` (`apps/runner/src/thread/tools/types.ts`). A refused call returns `{ content: <reason>, isError: true }`; every tool has `approval: 'never'`.

`listFilesTool(ctx)` → `list_files({ dir?, glob? })` (`tools/list-files.ts`): `git ls-files -z` in the worktree with one pathspec: `:(glob)<dir>/<glob>` when both are given, `:(glob)<dir>/**` for `dir` alone, `:(glob)<glob>` for `glob` alone, none for neither. `dir` passes `assertRelativePath`; `glob` matches `/^[A-Za-z0-9._*?\/\[\]{},-]{1,200}$/` and holds no `..`; a failing value is refused. Content: one path per line; above 2000 entries, the first 2000 and a last line `[truncated: <n> more]`; at most 262144 bytes (a cut list ends with `[truncated]`).

`searchRepoTool(ctx)` → `search_repo({ pattern, glob?, max?, fixed? })` (`tools/search-repo.ts`): `pattern` 1..1000 characters; `glob` the `list_files` rule; `max` an integer 1..200, default 200; another value of either is refused. `git -c core.quotePath=false grep -n -I --no-color` with `-F` when `fixed` is true, else `-E`, then `-e <pattern>`, then `-- :(glob)<glob>` when given; `env` `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`; `timeoutMs` `searchTimeoutMs`. Exit 0: hit lines `path:line:text`, at most `max` lines and at most 65536 bytes, a cut list ending with `[truncated]`. Exit 1: content `no matches`, no `isError`. Any other result: when `nowMs()` after the call is at least `searchTimeoutMs` past `nowMs()` before it, `isError` with content `search timed out`; else `isError` with git's first stderr line.

**Scope** — In: tool context and two read-only tracked-file tools over Git.run. Out: skill fetch (US-003), load_skill/read_skill_file and buildThreadTools (US-004). `write_doc`, Publish, untracked docs in `list_files` and `search_repo`, a stale session start and Discard belong to phase C. Note that nax-agent's own Read/Glob/Grep can see untracked files and its read-only Git can inspect history; the tracked-only rule applies to these two new tools, not to the agent.

**Interface** — `listFilesTool(ctx)` → `list_files({ dir?, glob? })`; `searchRepoTool(ctx)` → `search_repo({ pattern, glob?, max?, fixed? })`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: Given tracked a.ts, untracked b.ts and ignored c.log in a temp repository, listFilesTool(ctx).run({}) returns content whose lines are exactly ['a.ts'].
AC-2: Given tracked src/x.ts and docs/y.md, listFilesTool(ctx).run({ dir: 'src' }) returns content whose lines are exactly ['src/x.ts'].
AC-3: Given tracked src/x.ts and docs/y.md, listFilesTool(ctx).run({ glob: '**/*.md' }) returns content whose lines are exactly ['docs/y.md'].
AC-4: When listFilesTool(ctx).run({ dir: '../outside' }) is called, then it returns isError true.
AC-5: When listFilesTool(ctx).run({ glob: 'src/../..' }) is called, then it returns isError true.
AC-6: Given 2005 tracked files, listFilesTool(ctx).run({}) returns 2001 lines with last line '[truncated: 5 more]'.
AC-7: Given tracked src/a.ts with 'needle' on line 3, searchRepoTool(ctx).run({ pattern: 'needle' }) returns content whose first line starts 'src/a.ts:3:'.
AC-8: Given tracked lines 'a.b' and 'axb', searchRepoTool(ctx).run({ pattern: 'a.b', fixed: true }) returns exactly one hit line.
AC-9: Given 20 matching lines, searchRepoTool(ctx).run({ pattern: 'x', max: 5 }) returns exactly 5 hit lines followed by '[truncated]'.
AC-10: Given 300 matching lines, searchRepoTool(ctx).run({ pattern: 'x' }) returns exactly 200 hit lines followed by '[truncated]'.
AC-11: Given 150 matching lines of 1000 characters, searchRepoTool(ctx).run({ pattern: 'x' }) returns content of at most 65536 bytes.
AC-12: Given 150 matching lines of 1000 characters, searchRepoTool(ctx).run({ pattern: 'x' }) returns content whose last line is '[truncated]'.
AC-13: When no tracked file matches 'absent', searchRepoTool(ctx).run({ pattern: 'absent' }) returns content 'no matches' with isError not true.
AC-14: Given ctx.git.run resolves { code: 137 } and ctx.nowMs advances by searchTimeoutMs, searchRepoTool(ctx).run({ pattern: 'x' }) returns isError true with content 'search timed out'.
AC-15: When only a tracked binary file contains 'needle', searchRepoTool(ctx).run({ pattern: 'needle' }) returns content 'no matches'.

routing.reasoning: Two conventional git-backed read tools and a context type fit four files, but rejection of unsafe pathspecs is an access-control boundary requiring security-isolated TDD.

userStories.title: SHA-pinned public skill fetch and cache
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fetch validated SHA-pinned public GitHub skill sources to reusable isolated cache trees and prune old snapshots.

**Motivation** — The runner lacks skill tools and a safe way to supply reusable skill content to agent sessions.

**Approach** — `ensureSkills({ skills, skillsRoot, git, timeoutMs, origin?, maxTreeBytes? }): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: 'skill_fetch_failed' }>` (`apps/runner/src/thread/skill-fetch.ts`). `skillsRoot` is `<RunnerHome.dir>/skills`; `origin` defaults to `https://github.com` (tests pass a `file://` origin); `maxTreeBytes` defaults to 52428800. First every source is validated: `sourceId` `assertSegment`, `owner` `assertOwner`, `repo` `assertSegment`, `sha` `/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/`, each skill `dir` `assertRelativePath`; a failure returns `skill_fetch_failed` before any git call. Then for each source, `skillCacheDirFor(...)` holding a `.koda-complete` marker is reused and its mtime set to now. Otherwise, in a sibling temporary directory: `git init`; `git -c credential.helper= -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null fetch --depth 1 --no-recurse-submodules <origin>/<owner>/<repo> <sha>`; `git checkout --detach <sha>`; every call with `env` `{ GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0', GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE: '1' }` and `timeoutMs`; then the `.git` directory is deleted, the tree's total file size is checked against `maxTreeBytes` (after the fetch, not during it), the marker is written, and the directory is renamed into place (a target that appeared meanwhile wins; the temporary directory is deleted). Any failure deletes the temporary directory and returns `skill_fetch_failed`.

`pruneSkillCache(skillsRoot, now, maxAgeDays = 30)` deletes `<sourceId>/<sha>` directories whose mtime is more than `maxAgeDays` days before `now`.

**Scope** — In: fetch, marker-based reuse and age prune. Out: skill reading/tool set (US-004), daemon scheduling of prune (B3b); no git token is persisted in cache.

**Interface** — `ensureSkills({ skills, skillsRoot, git, timeoutMs, origin?, maxTreeBytes? }): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: 'skill_fetch_failed' }>`; `pruneSkillCache(skillsRoot, now, maxAgeDays = 30)`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: Given one source at a SHA of a file:// origin repository, ensureSkills returns { ok: true }.
AC-2: Given a successful ensureSkills for one source, then <skillsRoot>/<sourceId>/<sha>/<dir>/SKILL.md exists.
AC-3: When ensureSkills runs a second time for the same source, then it makes no git.run call whose arguments include 'fetch'.
AC-4: When ensureSkills runs a second time for a source whose cache directory mtime is 10 days old, then it sets that mtime to the current time.
AC-5: When ensureSkills fetches a source, then the fetch git.run call receives env.GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT '0'.
AC-6: When ensureSkills fetches a source, then the fetch git.run call receives arguments containing 'credential.helper=' after '-c'.
AC-7: Given successful ensureSkills, then <skillsRoot>/<sourceId>/<sha>/.git does not exist.
AC-8: Given a SHA absent from the origin, ensureSkills returns { ok: false, reason: 'skill_fetch_failed' }.
AC-9: Given a SHA absent from the origin, when ensureSkills completes, then <skillsRoot>/<sourceId> holds no entry.
AC-10: Given maxTreeBytes 10 and a skill tree larger than 10 bytes, ensureSkills returns { ok: false, reason: 'skill_fetch_failed' }.
AC-11: Given a source whose sha is '--upload-pack=x', ensureSkills returns { ok: false, reason: 'skill_fetch_failed' } without any git.run call.
AC-12: Given a source whose skill dir is '../escape', ensureSkills returns { ok: false, reason: 'skill_fetch_failed' } without any git.run call.
AC-13: Given a <sourceId>/<sha> cache directory whose mtime is 31 days before now, pruneSkillCache(skillsRoot, now) deletes it.
AC-14: Given a <sourceId>/<sha> cache directory whose mtime is 1 day before now, pruneSkillCache(skillsRoot, now) keeps it.

routing.reasoning: Untrusted server identifiers plus git credential isolation and external-source access require security-isolated TDD; caching and concurrent rename raise risk.

userStories.title: Jailed skill tools and assembled tool set
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add two safe skill-reading tools and assemble the four agent tools in a stable order.

**Motivation** — The runner has no code-search or skill tools for a brainstorm-thread agent.

**Approach** — `loadSkillTool(ctx)` → `load_skill({ name })` (`tools/load-skill.ts`): `name` must be a skill of `ctx.skills` (the first source listing it, in snapshot order), else `isError` with content `unknown skill <name>; available: <names, comma-separated>`. Returns the text of `<skill directory>/SKILL.md` under the `read_skill_file` file rules.

`readSkillFileTool(ctx)` → `read_skill_file({ name, relPath })` (`tools/read-skill-file.ts`): `relPath` passes `assertRelativePath`; the file's realpath is inside the skill directory's realpath; a symbolic link (`lstat`) is refused; above 262144 bytes is refused; a NUL byte or invalid UTF-8 is refused as binary. Each refusal is `isError` with a reason naming the rule.

`buildThreadTools(ctx): EmbedderTool[]` (`tools/index.ts`) returns, in order, `list_files`, `search_repo`, `load_skill`, `read_skill_file`. Each criterion runs over a skill directory laid out as `ensureSkills` leaves it (`<skillsRoot>/<sourceId>/<sha>/<dir>`). A refused call returns `{ content: <reason>, isError: true }`; every tool has `approval: 'never'`. The nax-agent built-in native read tools use a realpath jail to `workdir` (the worktree), keeping `~/.nax`, `~/.ssh` and `~/.koda-runner` outside it unreachable; these separate skill-file tools use the skill-directory realpath jail above.

**Scope** — In: skill file jail, tool approval settings and assembly of US-002 repo tools. Out: downloading/pruning cache (US-003), thread session construction (US-006). `write_doc`, Publish, untracked docs in `list_files` and `search_repo`, a stale session start and Discard belong to phase C.

**Interface** — `loadSkillTool(ctx)` → `load_skill({ name })`; `readSkillFileTool(ctx)` → `read_skill_file({ name, relPath })`; `buildThreadTools(ctx): EmbedderTool[]`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: Given a prepared skill directory, loadSkillTool(ctx).run({ name: 'spec-writing' }) returns content equal to its SKILL.md text.
AC-2: When loadSkillTool(ctx).run({ name: 'missing' }) is called, then it returns isError true with content naming every skill of ctx.skills.
AC-3: Given a prepared skill directory, readSkillFileTool(ctx).run({ name, relPath: 'references/guide.md' }) returns content equal to that file's text.
AC-4: When readSkillFileTool(ctx).run({ name, relPath: '../other/SKILL.md' }) is called, then it returns isError true.
AC-5: When readSkillFileTool(ctx).run(...) targets a symbolic link inside the skill directory, then it returns isError true.
AC-6: When readSkillFileTool(ctx).run(...) targets a file containing a NUL byte, then it returns isError true.
AC-7: When readSkillFileTool(ctx).run(...) targets a 262145-byte text file, then it returns isError true.
AC-8: When buildThreadTools(ctx) is called, then its tool names in order are ['list_files', 'search_repo', 'load_skill', 'read_skill_file'].
AC-9: When buildThreadTools(ctx) is called, then every returned tool has approval 'never'.

routing.reasoning: Three small tool modules assemble upstream helpers, but the skill-file realpath/symlink jail is an access-control boundary requiring security-isolated TDD.

userStories.title: Locked detached thread worktree and archive prune
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Create and refresh isolated per-thread worktrees without rewriting existing-clone configuration or blocking existing-clone jobs on the mutex, and remove archived registrations.

**Motivation** — The runner has no way to keep the agent inside a repo checkout without disturbing PLAN and RUN jobs that share the clone.

**Approach** — `prepareThreadWorktree({ git, mutex, repoKey, repoDir, cloneUrl, identity, credentialHelper, homeDir, threadId, baseRef, feature }): Promise<{ ok: true; worktree: string; tipSha: string } | { ok: false; reason: string }>` (`apps/runner/src/thread/thread-worktree.ts`); `feature` passes `assertFeature`. In order:

1. Clone missing (no `<repoDir>/.git`): acquire `mutex` for `repoKey`, check again, `ensureClone(...)`, release. Clone present: neither the mutex nor `ensureClone`.
2. `git fetch origin` in `repoDir` with `credentialHelper` passed on the command; a failure whose stderr contains `cannot lock ref` or `unable to lock` is retried once.
3. Tip: `refs/heads/feat/<feature>` when it exists in the clone, else `resolveRef(git, repoDir, baseRef)`; not found → `checkout: ref not found`; invalid → `checkout: invalid ref`.
4. Write `thread.json` `{ repoDir }` (before the worktree exists, so a crash never leaves a registration prune cannot find).
5. `git worktree list --porcelain`; an entry matches when `realpath(dirname(entry)) + '/' + basename(entry)` equals the same form of `wt` (a deleted directory cannot be realpathed itself):
   - registered and directory present → `git checkout --detach <tipSha>` inside it; git refusing → `worktree_conflict`;
   - registered and directory missing → `git worktree remove --force --force <wt>`, then add as below;
   - not registered → remove any leftover directory, then `git worktree add --detach --lock --reason koda-thread <wt> <tipSha>`.

Other git failures map through `reasonFromError`.

`pruneArchivedThreads({ git, homeDir, threadIds, activeThreadIds })` handles each id not in `activeThreadIds` (an id that fails `assertSegment` is skipped): it reads `thread.json`, and when `repoDir` is an absolute path with a `.git` it runs `git worktree remove --force --force <wt>` there (a failure ignored); then it deletes the thread directory.

**Scope** — In: mutex-only-for-clone initialization, per-command credential helper on fetch, unchanged helper configuration of an existing clone, detached locked worktree and prune function. Out: Wiring these blocks into the daemon (protocol v4, `THREAD` ASSIGN parsing, the `threadBackends` capability report, the thread job run, thread commands, Supervisor READOPT and ABANDON for `THREAD` rows, free slots, the heartbeat, `configureCredentials`, registering the `thread` stream with `LogShipper`, running `pruneArchivedThreads` and `pruneSkillCache`) belongs to feature `fleet-s5a-thread-host` (B3b).

**Interface** — `prepareThreadWorktree({ git, mutex, repoKey, repoDir, cloneUrl, identity, credentialHelper, homeDir, threadId, baseRef, feature }): Promise<{ ok: true; worktree: string; tipSha: string } | { ok: false; reason: string }>`; `pruneArchivedThreads({ git, homeDir, threadIds, activeThreadIds })`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: Given a temp clone without feat/<feature>, prepareThreadWorktree returns ok true with tipSha equal to the SHA of origin/<baseRef>.
AC-2: After prepareThreadWorktree, git worktree list --porcelain in the clone marks the wt entry 'locked'.
AC-3: After prepareThreadWorktree, git symbolic-ref -q HEAD in the worktree exits non-zero.
AC-4: Given a temp clone with local refs/heads/feat/<feature>, prepareThreadWorktree returns tipSha equal to that branch's SHA.
AC-5: When prepareThreadWorktree is called a second time after origin/<baseRef> moves, then it returns tipSha equal to the new SHA.
AC-6: When prepareThreadWorktree is called a second time after origin/<baseRef> moves, then the worktree HEAD equals the new SHA.
AC-7: Given a wt registered as a worktree but deleted from disk, prepareThreadWorktree returns ok true.
AC-8: Given a baseRef missing from the clone, prepareThreadWorktree returns { ok: false, reason: 'checkout: ref not found' }.
AC-9: Given an untracked file in the worktree that the new tip tracks with other content, prepareThreadWorktree returns { ok: false, reason: 'worktree_conflict' }.
AC-10: Given an existing clone, prepareThreadWorktree never calls mutex.acquire.
AC-11: Given no clone, prepareThreadWorktree calls mutex.acquire with repoKey.
AC-12: Given an existing clone and a credentialHelper, prepareThreadWorktree leaves the clone's git config --get-all credential.helper output unchanged.
AC-13: Given threadIds ['t1'] and no activeThreadIds, pruneArchivedThreads deletes <homeDir>/threads/t1.
AC-14: Given threadIds ['t1'] and no activeThreadIds, after pruneArchivedThreads git worktree list --porcelain in the clone lists no entry for t1's wt.
AC-15: Given threadIds ['t1'] and activeThreadIds ['t1'], pruneArchivedThreads keeps <homeDir>/threads/t1.

routing.reasoning: Concurrent shared-clone operations, durable worktree registration and credential-helper isolation make this high-risk and security-critical.

userStories.title: Read-profile native agent session factory
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Open or resume only native read-profile agent sessions with verified model choices, tools and file transcripts.

**Motivation** — The runner has no agent session library or way to host a brainstorm-thread session yet.

**Approach** — `ThreadSessionFactory` (`apps/runner/src/thread/session-factory.ts`), constructed with `{ homeDir, naxHome, nativeModels: () => Promise<NativeModelSet>, agent? }`; `agent` defaults to nax-agent's `{ createAgentSession, resumeAgentSession, nativeBackend, createFileTranscriptStore }`. `open({ jobId, thread: ThreadAssign, worktree, tools, approvalTimeoutSec }): Promise<{ ok: true; session: AgentSession; resumed: boolean } | { ok: false; reason: ThreadFailReason }>`:

1. `backend.kind === 'acp'` → `backend_unavailable` (B3-R9); nothing else is called.
2. Model: `backend.model ?? defaultModel`; null, not in `models`, or a `backend.effort` that fails `/^[a-z]{1,16}$/` → `model_unknown`.
3. `threadId` must match `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$/` (nax-agent's session id rule), else `session_error`.
4. `backend = nativeBackend({ model: effort ? '<model>[<effort>]' : model, carryHistoryAcrossModels: true, hostPorts: { protectedPaths: { gitExcludePathspecs: [], gitIgnorePatterns: [], credentialDir: naxHome } } })`.
5. Options: `backend`, `profile: 'read'` (no input changes it), `workdir: worktree`, `instructions: thread.instructions`, `tools`, `transcriptStore: createFileTranscriptStore(threadTranscriptDir(homeDir, threadId))`, `approvalTimeoutMs` = `approvalTimeoutSec * 1000` clamped to 30000..3600000, `turnTimeoutSeconds: 900`, `metadata: { threadId, jobId }`.
6. `resume: false` → `createAgentSession({ ...options, sessionId: threadId })`; `AGENT_SESSION_EXISTS` → `resumeAgentSession(threadId, options)`, `resumed: true`. `resume: true` → `resumeAgentSession(threadId, options)`; `AGENT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` (runner home wiped) → `createAgentSession`, `resumed: false`.
7. Errors from steps 4-6 (including a throw from `nativeBackend`): `AGENT_SESSION_AUTH_REQUIRED` → `agent_not_logged_in`; `AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE` → `backend_unavailable`; any other → `session_error`.

**Scope** — In: injected agent seam, native-only model resolution, protected paths settings, persisted transcripts and resume fallbacks. Out: daemon host/session lifecycle and configuring credentials (B3b). ACP session backends belong to phase D. A runtime nax-agent version-floor constant is not added (B3-R3); raising the pin is a manual dependency change.

**Interface** — `ThreadSessionFactory({ homeDir, naxHome, nativeModels: () => Promise<NativeModelSet>, agent? })`; `open({ jobId, thread: ThreadAssign, worktree, tools, approvalTimeoutSec }): Promise<{ ok: true; session: AgentSession; resumed: boolean } | { ok: false; reason: ThreadFailReason }>`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: Given resume false, ThreadSessionFactory.open calls injected createAgentSession with profile 'read'.
AC-2: Given resume true, ThreadSessionFactory.open calls injected resumeAgentSession with profile 'read'.
AC-3: When ThreadSessionFactory.open creates a session, then createAgentSession receives workdir equal to the given worktree.
AC-4: When ThreadSessionFactory.open creates a session, then injected createFileTranscriptStore receives <homeDir>/threads/<threadId>/transcript.
AC-5: Given resume false, ThreadSessionFactory.open calls createAgentSession with sessionId equal to thread.threadId.
AC-6: When ThreadSessionFactory.open creates a session, then createAgentSession receives backend equal to the injected nativeBackend return value.
AC-7: Given backend { kind: 'native', model: 'm/x', effort: 'high' } and models containing 'm/x', ThreadSessionFactory.open calls nativeBackend with model 'm/x[high]'.
AC-8: Given backend { kind: 'native' } and defaultModel 'm/b', ThreadSessionFactory.open calls nativeBackend with model 'm/b'.
AC-9: When ThreadSessionFactory.open constructs a native backend, then nativeBackend receives carryHistoryAcrossModels true.
AC-10: Given backend model 'm/z' absent from models, ThreadSessionFactory.open returns { ok: false, reason: 'model_unknown' } without calling createAgentSession.
AC-11: Given backend { kind: 'native' } and defaultModel null, ThreadSessionFactory.open returns { ok: false, reason: 'model_unknown' }.
AC-12: Given backend { kind: 'acp', agent: 'claude' }, ThreadSessionFactory.open returns { ok: false, reason: 'backend_unavailable' } without calling nativeBackend.
AC-13: Given resume true and resumeAgentSession throws AgentSessionError with code AGENT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND, ThreadSessionFactory.open returns ok true with resumed false.
AC-14: Given resume false and createAgentSession throws AgentSessionError with code AGENT_SESSION_EXISTS, ThreadSessionFactory.open returns ok true with resumed true.
AC-15: Given createAgentSession throws AgentSessionError with code AGENT_SESSION_AUTH_REQUIRED, ThreadSessionFactory.open returns { ok: false, reason: 'agent_not_logged_in' }.

routing.reasoning: Agent sessions, credentials/auth mapping and mandatory read-only profile are security-critical, with injection and transcript fallback complexity.

userStories.title: Redacted capped thread event stream writer
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Serialize native agent session events and runner lifecycle lines to an append-only redacted, byte-bounded thread stream with paced log wakes.

**Motivation** — The runner has no safe way to report what the agent says, and redacting each small delta alone misses secrets split across deltas.

**Approach** — `new ThreadEventWriter({ path, jobId, leaseEpoch, logs, wakeGapMs, now, sleep, streamMaxBytes?, onCap, onWarn })` (`apps/runner/src/thread/thread-event-writer.ts`); `path` is the stream file, created with mode 0600 if absent and appended to otherwise; `streamMaxBytes` defaults to `THREAD_STREAM_LIMITS.streamMaxBytes`; `bytes()` is the file's size. Methods, all returning `void`: `event(e: SessionEvent)`, `started({ resumed, backend, skillShas })`, `inputConsumed(messageId)`, `closed(reason)`, `failed(reason)`, `flush()`.

- Held delta text (B3-R11): `text_delta` text is appended to a raw buffer keyed by `(turnId, round)`. After each append, the writable prefix ends at the last whitespace character that sits at least 256 characters before the buffer's end (none → nothing is written yet, unless the buffer passes 4096 characters, when the prefix is all but its last 256 characters). The prefix is passed through `redactSecrets` and written as `text_delta` lines; the rest stays raw. The held text is written, redacted, before any other session line (a `text_delta` of another round, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `usage`, `turn_end` and the rest), and on `flush()`; a `stream_reset` of the round drops it and is then written.
- `thinking_delta.text`, `turn_end.output` and `turn_end.error.message` are each passed through `redactSecrets` whole. Splitting into lines happens after redaction.
- Wake: after each append `logs.wake(jobId, leaseEpoch)`, at most once per `wakeGapMs`, plus one trailing wake after the gap for appends inside it.
- Cap: before each session line, `bytes() + lineBytes > streamMaxBytes - 4096` → that line and the rest of its event are not written and `onCap()` is called (once per writer); runner lines (`started`, `inputConsumed`, `closed`, `failed`) are always written.

Stream contract (for B2): one JSON object per line, UTF-8, `\n`-terminated; a line's size is the byte length of its serialized JSON plus the newline, at most `THREAD_STREAM_LIMITS.lineMaxBytes`. Session lines keep nax-agent's `SessionEvent` fields (`type`, `sessionId`, `turnId`, `at`, `metadata`, body), in the order the session produced them. `text_delta.text`, `thinking_delta.text`, `turn_end.output` and `turn_end.error.message` are redacted as below; `tool_call.input`, `tool_result.preview`, `question.text` and approval summaries carry nax-agent's own best-effort redaction. A `text_delta` too long for one line becomes several `text_delta` lines with the same `turnId` and `round`, in order. A `turn_end` too long for one line is written with `output: ""` and `outputTruncated: true`. Any other session line too long for one line is dropped and reported through the writer's `onWarn`. `stream_reset` lines are written.

**Scope** — In: local file writer, session/runner JSONL, delta redaction, line/stream caps and wake pacing. Out: registering the thread log stream with LogShipper and uploads (B3b/B2); do not add sync log events or additional nax-agent field redaction. The API accepting and folding the `thread` stream, and an API parity test pinning `THREAD_MODEL_ID_RE` to the API's `MODEL_ID_RE`, belong to feature `fleet-s5a-thread-ingest` (B2). `tool_call.input`, `tool_result.preview`, `question.text` and approval summaries rely on nax-agent's best-effort redaction; this feature adds none.

**Interface** — `new ThreadEventWriter({ path, jobId, leaseEpoch, logs, wakeGapMs, now, sleep, streamMaxBytes?, onCap, onWarn })`; `bytes()`; `event(e: SessionEvent)`, `started({ resumed, backend, skillShas })`, `inputConsumed(messageId)`, `closed(reason)`, `failed(reason)`, `flush()`; all methods other than `bytes()` return `void`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: Given two text_delta events of one round containing 'key: ' plus the first half of an Anthropic-style API key and then its second half, followed by turn_end, ThreadEventWriter writes text_delta lines whose texts joined in file order equal nax-agent redactSecrets of the whole text.

AC-2: Given a text_delta of 1000 characters made of 9-letter words separated by single spaces, ThreadEventWriter writes text_delta lines before any further event whose texts joined are a prefix of the original ending in a space and at most 744 characters long.
AC-3: Given a text_delta of 100 characters then a tool_call of the same turn, ThreadEventWriter writes the line carrying those 100 characters before the tool_call line.
AC-4: Given a stream_reset of a round after a 100-character text_delta of that round, ThreadEventWriter writes no line carrying those 100 characters.
AC-5: Given a turn_end whose output contains an Anthropic-style API key, ThreadEventWriter writes a line whose output equals nax-agent redactSecrets of that output.
AC-6: Given a turn_end whose error.message contains an Anthropic-style API key, ThreadEventWriter writes a line whose error.message equals nax-agent redactSecrets of that message.
AC-7: Given a thinking_delta whose text contains an Anthropic-style API key, ThreadEventWriter writes a line whose text equals nax-agent redactSecrets of that text.
AC-8: Given a 200000-character text_delta of words containing 'é' followed by turn_end, ThreadEventWriter writes only lines whose UTF-8 byte length including newline is at most 65536.
AC-9: Given a 200000-character text_delta of words separated by spaces followed by turn_end, ThreadEventWriter writes text_delta lines whose texts joined in file order equal the original text.
AC-10: Given a turn_end with output of 100000 characters, ThreadEventWriter writes one turn_end line with output '' and outputTruncated true.

AC-11: When ThreadEventWriter.started({ resumed: false, backend: { kind: 'native', model: 'm/x' }, skillShas: ['<sha>'] }) is called, then it writes an object deep-equal to { type: 'session_started', at: <now ISO>, resumed: false, backend: { kind: 'native', model: 'm/x' }, skillShas: ['<sha>'] }.
AC-12: When ThreadEventWriter.inputConsumed('msg1') is called, then it writes an object deep-equal to { type: 'input_consumed', at: <now ISO>, messageId: 'msg1' }.
AC-13: Given ten thinking_delta event calls within one wakeGapMs on a manual clock, when the clock advances past wakeGapMs, then logs.wake is called exactly twice.

AC-14: Given streamMaxBytes 8192 and a pre-seeded 4200-byte stream file, when two 100-character thinking_delta events are given, then ThreadEventWriter writes neither line and calls onCap exactly once.
AC-15: Given streamMaxBytes 8192 and a pre-seeded 4200-byte stream file, ThreadEventWriter.closed('stream_cap') writes the session_closed line.
